rows.why: A single bare brown stick with three orange oval leaves; no clump of slender ringed stems, no feather-frond crown, no hanging berry brooms — none of the three must-reads exists.

An arching fountain of pale blades like ornamental grass; culms droop instead of standing tall and jointed, leaves run the whole length, and there is no brown-sheathed cone shoot at the base — the harvest itself is absent.

An upright twiggy fan with berries in clusters at the tips — the packet's own separator from blueberry is solitary axillary berries, and the 'low dense mound of green twigs' is instead a tall sparse skeleton; construction is near-identical to the Juniper Berries tile.

Generic round-crown tree with smooth brown ball fruit — the identity must-reads (huge hand-lobed leaves, green soft-spined fruit) are both missing, and it is plainly the same tree construction as Date Plum with browner fruit.
Broad rounded dome crown with large glossy radiating leaves and small dark berries is there; the three-veined leaf detail and fissured bark are not readable — the trunk is a plain smooth brown.
A fern, but the must-read rock crevice it spills from is completely absent (it sits on bare ground), and it is the same splayed frond-mound construction as Hardy Fern with only a darker green.

A dense leafy column like a mullein with an orange tuft on top — the spec is one short stem, one or two big crumpled lobed leaves, one solitary amber berry; nothing of that single-stem herb reads here.

White puffs on a bare green stem do suggest cotton, but the plant has zero leaves (3-5 lobed leaves are a must-read), no split brown boll husks around the fluff, and no cream flower — two of three must-reads missing outright.
Tree with round crown and small orange persimmon-like fruit reads right; the dark blocky bark is a plain smooth trunk and the papery star calyx on the fruit is not visible at this scale.
Grey-green lobed leaves and a small mottled round melon are both present, but the vine climbs diagonally instead of trailing flat on sand, and no yellow flowers are visible.
Formless horizontal mat of hair-fine tangled green filaments with no stem or holdfast reads correctly; the trapped gas bubbles lifting the mat are not visible.

The must-read shuttlecock rosette of upright fronds is instead a sideways sprawling mound — the identical construction to the Cave Fern tile with only a lighter green, which is the hue-swap clone case.

All three must-reads land — gold-brown staining under the ice, stringy amber mucilage strands trailing into the water, no plant structure — but the ice itself is a hard-edged flat gradient rectangle rather than sea ice.

Needle ticks on the twigs and blue-black berry clusters are present, but the bush is a sparse upright twig fan rather than the dense scruffy conical mound, and it sits close to the Bilberry silhouette.

Generic round-crown tree on a plain straight trunk — no arching stilt roots, no water, no hanging cigar-shaped propagules; all three must-reads absent, and it is the same tree construction as Neem/Wild Mango with the fruit removed.

Drawn as an upright S-curved climbing vine with the small netted fruit dangling mid-air; the must-reads say ground-trailing runner and fruit resting on the ground — its neighbour Watermelon shows the correct horizontal construction, making the miss obvious.

Broad rounded crown with feathery drooping pinnate sprays clearly visible; the pale yellow balls in the crown read as the olive-like fruit, but the loose sprays of small white flowers are not distinguishable as sprays.

Needle bundles radiate clearly from the crown and the trunk is bare, so it reads as a pine, but the crown is a rounded puff rather than the flat umbrella, and the stout rounded cones are only vague tan blobs.

The vivid red stalks fanning from a ground crown are right, but every leaf is a small smooth lollipop circle — the huge crinkled heart-shaped blades (a must-read, and the size relation 'leaves far larger than expected') are plainly wrong.
A single blue-grey fountain tuft — no spreading runners, no two-ranked comb leaves, no seed head at all; it is the same tuft construction as Tussock Grass beside it with only the hue changed.

Silvery narrow willow leaves and orange berry clusters are both present and read as sea buckthorn, but the berries sit in loose blossom-like heads at the stem tips instead of packed tight directly along the thorny twig.

Multi-stemmed shrub with small leaves and scattered purple-blue berries reads correctly; the strap-petal white flowers are not visible and the starry crown scar on the berries is invisible at this scale.
Unmistakable: huge veined ovate leaves stepping up a single stout stem, shrinking toward the top, crowned by a cluster of pink trumpet flowers — a stranger names it immediately.

Straw-tan fountain of arching blades with longer thin wisps above that read as seed panicles, but the raised pedestal mound of dead thatch is missing — the base narrows to a point — and there is no green-above/tan-below split.

Horizontal ground-trailing runner with a coiled tendril, deeply lobed grey-green leaves, and a round melon with visible darker green stripes sitting flat on the ground — all three must-reads present and nameable.

Wiry many-branched upright bush with scarlet round fruits held upward at the tips reads as a chili bush, but the small white star flowers are absent and the fruits run cherry-sized rather than pea-sized.

Dense green crown with pear-shaped yellow-orange fruits, one dangling at the crown edge, reads as a mango tree; but the long dangling fruit stalks are barely visible — fruits sit mostly embedded on the crown surface.

An open wispy multi-stem shrub with red dot berries — the must-read dense evergreen small-tree crown is missing, the holly-like leathery leaves are indistinct, and it is essentially Serviceberry's construction with the dots recoloured red.
Lumpy no-stem nuggets with cut face present, but white veins are sparse straight scratches not marbled lace, and the pyramidal warts are illegible on the purple rind.
Dense bouquet of long needle-thin white stems fused at the base reads clearly, but several caps are small bells noticeably wider than the stems instead of tiny pinheads.
Two smooth opaque orange spheres with scribbled lines on top: no 3D brain-like folds, no translucency, no bark — reads as fruit, all three must-reads missing.
Conical honeycomb head on cream stalk is nameable, but the pits are a flat uniform diamond-grid pattern with no recessed depth, and the head slightly overhangs the stalk like a cap.

Reads clearly as a centipede — many identical segments, legs fanned along both sides, antennae and rear trailing legs present — but the body is a chain of rounded beads, not the flattened profile the must-read calls for.

The grossly unequal claws now read — one large open-pincer claw dwarfs the tiny opposite one — and eye stalks stand up off the carapace, but the stalks are stubby pins rather than long, and only two or three walking legs are visible.
Strong woodlouse read (overlapping armour bands, bent antennae, row of small legs), but the rear plate rounds off smooth with no uropods visible flanking it — a must-read is missing.

Long trailing antennae are present, but the curled segmented abdomen ends in a blunt rounded tip with no fanned tail, and no rostrum spike shows between the eyes — two must-reads invisible; the tight curl reads more like a curled larva than a shrimp.
Only dorsal lobe sits right behind the head, not far back; no tusk pair on the lower jaw (lone pale wedge is at the beak tip); tail frays into fish-like filament spikes instead of a fluke.
Notched whale fluke present and no dorsal fin, downturned blunt muzzle reads; but odd vertical rib ridge lines cross the body and the bristly snout disc is faint.
Rounded paddle tail clearly distinct from the dugong's notched fluke, barrel body with front flipper; but the paddle has fish-fin rays and the split upper lip is not visible.

Fruit reads as apples — large pale-green/yellow rounds with an apple shine, one dangling low; no spines at the leaf joints and no winged leaf stalks anywhere in the soft hazy (not dark glossy) crown, so two must-reads are invisible.

Salmon-pink round fruit among long narrow drooping willow-like leaves reads peach, but the fruit is a flat uniform dot with no cleft seam or red-over-gold blush, and the crown is a round ball on a tall bare trunk, not a low spreading vase.

The fruit are dark-green vertically striped ovals sitting inside a dense round crown — they read as little watermelons, not spiny heart-shaped soursops, and none hang from the trunk or thick branches; the small open crown must-read is also missing.

Upright black-back/white-front body, stubby wing tight to the flank, and rear-set feet are all present, but the bright yellow conical bill reads penguin/finch rather than a razorbill-type auk blade bill.

The must-read black cap is missing — the crown is entirely white — and the bird stands on planted legs over a ground shadow instead of the specified flying posture with long narrow pointed wings; only the slim dagger bill and a faint forked-tail shape are present.

Yellow near-circular disc body reads clearly, but the eye marking is a thin dark ring around the eye rather than a masking bar, and the snout is a stubby orange nub instead of a pointed tweezer snout — right species, secondary gaps.

Blue disc body and crescent-ish tail are there, but the sharp tail-base spine (a must-read) is invisible — the caudal peduncle is uniform blue-on-blue with no contrasting scalpel mark where the tail joins the body.

Rainbow comb stripes are present, but the body is an open-bottomed jellyfish BELL with two long curled trailing tentacles — the exact bell-plus-trailing-tentacles construction the note forbids; the 'transparent oval body, no stinging tentacles' must-read is wrong and a stranger names it jellyfish.

Spherical test with a dense halo of long straight spines reads instantly as a sea urchin, but the 'five-part radial pattern under the spines' must-read is invisible — the test shows only vague random smudges with no five-fold symmetry.

Ordered striae + raphe lattice is there, but the interior is empty dark — no golden-brown plastids showing through the shell — and there is no two-half pillbox seam; two of three must-reads invisible.

Full cilia fringe reads well, but the silhouette is a plain symmetric ellipse — no asymmetric slipper outline with a blunt end — and no diagonal oral groove cuts into the cell side; the defining silhouette must-read is missing.
Tiny pale body with head-length triangular ears reads fennec, but the ears render as messy overlapping shards and the black on the bushy tail sits at the base/ring rather than the tip.
Body is tall and horse-like on long straight legs instead of low and slender; tail is solid orange with no white tip and legs show no black stockings — two must-reads missing.

Tail is thin, round and tapering (curled behind the rump), not the broad flattened paddle the note demands; no cream throat bib — body is uniform tan; head is a raised knob with a stalk snout, not a flat whiskered otter head. Reads as dachshund/weasel.

Body is a plump oval covered in a prominent dotted SCALE texture, contradicting 'translucent scaleless tadpole body'; tail is a small separate fan, not fins merging into a tapering point; no belly sucker disc visible. Generic scaled fish.
Fat round body and near-invisible stub tail are there, but a distinct rounded ear stands visibly off the head instead of being buried in the coat, and the big white incisors read slightly hamster.

Long naked body-length tail, pink-inner ears and whiskers land the read, but the muzzle is the same blunt teeth-forward muzzle as the Lemming rather than a pointed snout, and the body is round-compact instead of the longer 2.6 proportion.
Tapered cigar-shaped ellipse, not a parallel-edged razor blade; no digging foot extends from either end — the shell is the whole drawing.
Fan ribs and hinge ears read correctly, but the must-read row of bright blue mantle eyes is invisible and no tentacle fringe shows between the valves.

Bill is horizontal, not the sky-pointing dagger of the reed-mimic freeze pose, and the neck is a thin curved tube instead of thick and hunched; only a hint of buff streaking survives, so it reads as a generic sandpiper-like wader.

Green-shoulder must-read is absent — the cone rim under the greens is the palest cream area, no green tint; root is buff-tan not orange (reads parsnip), ring marks invisible, and the 'fine side hairs' are three thick dark sticks on the lower-left flank.

Slender red-orange bill and bright red legs both visible on an all-dark bird, so the species reads; but the bill's curve is barely there, the red leans orange, and the body is a dumpy round blob with charcoal-grey rather than glossy black crow-like plumage.

Berries are drawn as upright terminal clusters crowning straight vertical stems — the must-read drooping string/raceme is absent (nothing hangs), and the narrow-fingered palmate leaves read hemp-like, not maple-like; a stranger would not name this currant.

Unmistakable: big fanned orange circular frill behind the head and a whip tail well over half the body length, sprawling stance. But the third must-read underdelivers — the mouth is a thin pink slit with white tooth zigzag, reading as a closed grimace rather than a wide GAPING pink gape at the frill's centre. Right species, one must-read soft.
Yellow band sits mid-body, not a collar behind the head, and the body is a closed donut coil instead of the required loose S-curve crawl; only the rounded head with round pupil reads correctly.

Plump standing gamebird (partridge/quail read), not a flying falcon: no hooked bill or moustache stripe, no black spotting on the back, short unbarred tail wedge, no pointed wings — every must-read absent.

Leaves float flat on the water like lily pads with no emergent stalks — the packet's explicit do-not-conflate case; no shower-head seed pod anywhere; the bloom is a tiny flat pink star, not a large cupped many-petalled bowl. All three must-reads missing.

Tail is a rounded club-tipped tube, not the laterally flattened paddle must-read; no salt crust on the snout and no visible claws — dorsal dots don't read as a spiny crest, so it reads as a dark salamander, not a marine iguana.

Unmistakable orange-red shag and a flange-like disc ring around the small pale face carry the species, but the arms hug the squat body at roughly body-width — the enormous arm span reads gorilla-stubby, and the cheek-flange ring is thin enough to pass for a hair rim.

Uniform pale cream body — no grizzled grey back or tawny legs — and the tail is short, sparse and carried up off the rump instead of a long bushy dark-tipped brush held low; only a vague dark ear patch, so it reads as a generic pale dog, not a pampas fox.

Big-headed big-eyed must-read absent: head is small against the body and the eye is a tiny dot, not prominent; body is horizontal, not compact-upright, with an odd concentric-ring disc pattern for a wing — reads as a small pigeon/dove, not a plover. Only the short stubby bill survives.

Five russet-red lobes with cream warty spots read well, but the mandatory deep central pit ringed with spikes is absent — the centre is a solid convex dark-red dome with a highlight, no opening and no spike ring visible.

No tuber drawn at all — the defining orange spindle-shaped harvest organ is absent; leaves are plain circles with no heart notch or lobes, and the stem climbs diagonally instead of trailing as ground-hugging runners. All three must-reads missing.
